texts.li: [lowtech] Midsummer is here, and {A_nameDef} has dragged half a dead tree into the yard for the fire. Back home, {A_nameDef} says, people jumped the midsummer fire for luck, and {A_pronoun} would like to try it here.\n\nIt would burn a good stack of firewood.

[!lowtech] The days are as long as they get. {A_nameDef} wants a bonfire to mark it, with the lamps off for once and everyone outside until the sky goes pale again.\n\nIt would burn a good stack of firewood.
[rain] It's midsummer and it has rained since breakfast, but {A_nameDef} still wants the bonfire tonight. {A_nameDef} has kept a stack of logs dry under the eaves for a week, just in case.

[trait:Pyromaniac] {A_nameDef} has a plan for a midsummer bonfire: where the logs go, how high, which way the wind will take the sparks. The council would rather {A_nameDef} lit it with permission than without.

[colony:Traditional] The colony keeps its seasons, and {A_nameDef} has asked that midsummer be kept too: a bonfire taller than the roof, singing, and the night shift let off until morning.\n\nThe woodpile would feel it.

lines.li: [lowtech] The fire burned until dawn, and {A_nameDef} jumped it three times for luck.
[rain] The rain let up an hour after sunset and the fire caught at the first try. They stayed out until the logs were ash.
The bonfire went up taller than the roof. {A_nameDef} was the last one to bed, and the first one asking about next year.
The logs went back on the woodpile. {A_nameDef} went to bed early, with the window open to the short night.
A small fire and an early night. {A_nameDef} sat up with the embers after the others had gone in.
[lowtech] A fire the size of a cartwheel, some stories, and bed. {A_nameDef} took a coal home in a pot, for luck.

texts.li: [lowtech] The last cart of the harvest came in at dusk. {A_nameDef}, who sowed most of it by hand, asks for a harvest supper tonight with everyone at one table. It would cost about {COUNT} raw food.
[!lowtech] The last of the crop is in the freezer, weighed and logged. {A_nameDef} would like one night of eating it before it all goes into storage: a harvest home, about {COUNT} raw food.

[trait:Gourmand] {A_nameDef} has been planning the harvest supper since the seedlings came up: what to roast, what to stew, who sits where. It would cost about {COUNT} raw food, and {A_nameDef} has already started peeling.

[colony:Thrifty] The harvest is in. {A_nameDef} knows this colony isn't one for feasts, and is asking anyway: one supper for the people who brought it in, about {COUNT} raw food.\n\nThe stores will have to last the winter either way.
[rain] The last field was harvested in the rain, and everyone who worked it is soaked and sore. {A_nameDef} asks for a harvest supper tonight, about {COUNT} raw food, and a fire to dry out by.

lines.li: The harvest home went on past midnight. {A_nameDef} got the first slice of everything and didn't share it.
[lowtech] They ate in the barn among the sacks, with lanterns hung from the beams. {A_nameDef} was toasted twice and sang once, badly.
Every sack went into storage. {A_nameDef} counted them twice and said nothing about supper.
The harvest is stored against the winter, all of it. {A_nameDef} still smells of the fields and has gone to bed hungry.
A good supper, nothing fancy, with a second helping for {A_nameDef}, who grew most of it.

texts.li: [lowtech] The longest night has come, and the hall fire is the only warm place left. {A_nameDef} wants to keep it the old way: everyone in one room, extra food, and a story from each.
[!lowtech] It's the longest night of the year and the heaters are struggling. {A_nameDef} thinks this is the night to bring everyone into one room, with extra rations and every lamp lit.

[snow] Snow has been falling since morning on the longest night of the year. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to mark it with extra food and a long evening together, before everyone scatters to their cold rooms.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} has been going room to room all evening with blankets. It's midwinter, {A_nameDef} tells the council, and no night to spend alone: could there be extra food and one big fire?

[colony:Traditional] Midwinter again. The colony has its ways for the longest night, and {A_nameDef} wants to know if the council means to keep them this year: extra rations and a long evening around the fire.

lines.li: [lowtech] They ate around the hearth until the logs burned down, and {A_nameDef} kept a candle going until morning.
[snow] They ate with the snow piling up against the door and didn't notice the cold until the plates were empty.
Extra rations and a long table. {A_nameDef} carved, and gave the biggest pieces away.
Stories around the hearth until late. {A_nameDef} told one about a winter back home, and a few people asked for it again.
The longest night came and went. {A_nameDef} spent it in {A_possessive} own room, under every blanket {A_pronoun} owns.

texts.li: Spring is here, and the colony wants a name for the new year. {A_nameDef} has suggested {A_possessive} own name and repeats it at every meal. The other favorites are the colony's dead and, for some reason, the muffalo.

[lowtech] By old custom the year gets its name at the first planting. {A_nameDef} has carved a candidate into the dining table: {A_possessive} own name. Someone else has carved a muffalo next to it.\n\nThe council has been asked to choose before the table runs out of room.

[trait:Jealous] {A_nameDef} heard that the year might be named after someone else and has started a campaign: {A_possessive} own name, written on a board by the door. Others want the year named for the dead. A few want the muffalo.

lines.li: It is the year of {A_nameDef}. {A_nameDef} has added it to the board by the door, in large letters.
The year is named for the colony's dead. {A_nameDef} read the names out at supper, and the table was quiet for a while after.
The year of the muffalo, then. Someone tied a ribbon to the muffalo's horn, and it ate the ribbon. {A_nameDef} is sulking.

texts.li: [lowtech] The raiders left more than bodies: good boots, a shield with only one crack in it, a bow {A_nameDef} has already restrung. {A_nameDef} brought down more of them than anyone and wants first pick.\n\nThe others want the council to decide.

[!lowtech] There's a rifle out there with a scope that still works, and {A_nameDef} has had an eye on it since the shooting stopped. {A_nameDef} hit more raiders than anyone and says that should count when the gear is shared out.\n\nThe others haven't agreed to anything yet.

[winter] The raiders came dressed for winter, and their coats are warmer than anything the colony owns. {A_nameDef}, who did most of the shooting, has asked for the best one. So has nearly everyone else.

[trait:Greedy] {A_nameDef} was out among the bodies before the smoke had cleared, sorting the gear into two piles: {A_possessive} pile and the rest. {A_nameDef} did most of the shooting and sees nothing wrong with it.\n\nThe others want the council to have a say.

[past:soldier] {A_nameDef} soldiered long enough to know how a company shares its spoils: whoever did the shooting chooses first. {A_nameDef} did most of it today.\n\nMost of the colony never served, and doesn't see it that way.

[past:outlaw] Where {A_nameDef} comes from, whoever drops a raider takes the raider's things. {A_nameDef} dropped more of them than anyone today and has started collecting.\n\nSome of the others want it stopped until the council has decided.

[colony:Generous] Everything taken from raiders goes into the common stores here; that's how the colony has always done it. This time {A_nameDef}, who shot more of them than anyone, wants first pick, and said so at supper.

lines.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} took the bow and the best boots. A few of the others grumble that they stood on the wall as well.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} took the scoped rifle and a decent jacket. The rest went to the stores, and some of the others say they fought too.
[trait:Greedy] {A_nameDef} took the best of the spoils and a fair share of the rest. Some of the others have stopped sitting with {A_objective} at meals.
Everything went into the common stores, the good boots along with the torn ones. {A_nameDef} thinks fair shares are fine for people who didn't do the shooting.
[colony:Generous] The spoils went to the common stores, as everything does here. {A_nameDef} knew that would be the answer and still looks sore about it.
[lowtech] Everyone who stood on the wall got a share. The ones who kept the fires and carried water got nothing, and some of them have said so.
The fighters divided the spoils on the dining table. The ones who stayed in to tend the wounded got the cleanup, and remember it.

texts.li: [winter] The raiders lie frozen where they fell, and the ground is too hard to dig without a long day of it. {A_nameDef} asks what the council wants done with them.
[summer|hot] It's hot, and the raiders lying outside the wall won't keep. {A_nameDef} wants the council to decide today: graves, a pyre, or the treeline.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} has covered the dead raiders' faces with their own coats and is asking for graves. The rest of the colony isn't sure they've earned the work.
[lowtech] The old custom is that the dead get their rites, whoever they were. Not everyone here keeps the old custom. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to decide what's done with the raiders' bodies.

[colony:Harsh] The colony isn't known for mercy, and the raiders' bodies are still where they fell. {A_nameDef} wants to know whether the council means to bury them, burn them, or leave them for the animals.
[rain] The raiders' bodies have been lying in the rain all night. {A_nameDef} has been out to look at them twice and wants a decision before the ground turns to mud.

lines.li: [winter] It took two days and a fire on the ground to soften it, but the raiders have graves now, in a row outside the wall.
The raiders are buried in a row outside the wall. {A_nameDef} put up a marker with nothing written on it.
[lowtech] The pyre burned through the night. By morning there was a black patch on the ground and the smell in everyone's clothes.
[rain] The pyre wouldn't take in the wet until someone poured lamp oil over it. It burned until dawn.
[winter] The bodies were hauled to the treeline and left in the snow. Animals found them the first night.
The bodies went to the treeline. {A_nameDef} didn't help carry them, and won't walk that way now.

texts.li: [lowtech] The raiders are gone and the gate held. {A_nameDef} wants a feast tonight with every torch lit. It would use about {COUNT} raw food, and the mending would wait until morning.
[winter] The raid is over, the wounded are inside, and it's bitterly cold. {A_nameDef} wants a hot feast for everyone tonight, about {COUNT} raw food, before anyone goes back out to fix the walls.

[colony:Hardworking] This colony usually goes straight back to work after a fight. {A_nameDef} wants it to be different this time: a feast tonight, about {COUNT} raw food, and the repairs in the morning.

[night] It's dark already, the raiders are gone, and the colony is too wound up to sleep. {A_nameDef} suggests a feast now, about {COUNT} raw food, while everyone is still awake and alive to enjoy it.

lines.li: [lowtech] They ate by torchlight in the yard, loud with relief. {A_nameDef} beat time on an upturned pot until well past midnight.
The feast went on well after dark. {A_nameDef} made a speech about the fight, and it got longer every time someone refilled {A_possessive} cup.
Back to work on the walls, the wounded and the bodies. {A_nameDef} worked through the night and said nothing more about a feast.
